subject: Private deployment: patch governance proposal & fast-revert plan
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: ops@greencliff.com, alice.kim@greencliff.com, vendor-ops@netsecure.io
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Private deployment: patch governance proposal & fast-revert plan

Hi all,

Summary: attached is a proposed maintenance governance plan for the Private (VPC/on‑prem) runtime upgrade we discussed last week. The goal is to push a security/compatibility patch to the customer-managed control plane and inference runtime with a verified fast‑revert path that minimizes customer impact.

Key highlights (high level):
- Target maintenance window: 2026-12-08 02:00–04:00 UTC (tentative) -- we still need confirmation from Greencliff.
- Scope: control-plane minor bump (0.9.7 -> 0.9.8), runtime binaries with new attention kernel, and a small config change to the KV cache invalidation TTL.
- Pinning: we will keep the pinned model revision for the tenant during the window; no automatic model upgrades.
- Canary: staged canary at 5% (two customer-serving pods) for 20 minutes before full rollout.
- Fast revert: snapshot-based revert of runtime containers + control-plane config restore; revert checklist attached (revert-checklist-v1.md).
- Network changes: a short ACL change for service egress to the telemetry collector (netflow-diagram.png included), vendor firewall update required.
- Audit & evidence: we will capture syslogs, API audit events, and a token-level cost/latency sample for the window.

Asks:
1) Greencliff: confirm acceptable window and whether they require a shorter blackout (they previously requested <= 2 hours).
2) NetSecure (vendor): confirm firewall rule commit lead and ETA for rule change in the proposed window.
3) Infra/Runtime (Irene/Karthik): quick review of the KV eviction change and the canary gating criteria — any missing rollback triggers?

Attachments: GC-maintenance-MAP-v1.2.pdf (full Mutual Action Plan), revert-checklist-v1.md, netflow-diagram.png.

If we have sign-off by EOD Thursday (2026-12-03), we can lock the window and send the final runbook + DocuSign approval for Greencliff.

Thanks,

Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment: patch governance proposal & fast-revert plan

Logan — thanks for drafting. Quick technical notes from runtime/ops perspective: we should tighten the rollback triggers and call out cache/coherency risks explicitly. A few concrete items below.

1) KV cache invalidation TTL change: the plan mentions reducing TTL from 15m -> 5m to avoid stale configs. This will increase spike in GC calls during the canary unless we wire a staggered start across nodes. Recommendation: stagger by node-start time (30s offsets) and add a soft‑throttle on cache eviction to avoid thundering herd. Add this as a pre-check and a gating metric (heap churn and eviction rate).

2) Model pinning confirmation: ensure the agent.json for the tenant has a pinned_model_revision entry before we touch runtime images. Don't rely on global defaults. If pin is missing, the revert path must include an explicit model pin operation prior to snapshot rollback.

3) Snapshot restore time: our last rehearsal shows a worst-case control-plane restore ~9 minutes (for the tenant DB subset). Add a single timeout threshold: if revert not completed in 30 minutes escalate to ops-lead and hold traffic.

4) Network ACL change: vendor needs to commit the new egress rule + a temporary allowlist for telemetry host x.x.56.12. If vendor can't commit timely, we will keep telemetry as-is for the window (means no post-rollback sampling).

5) Health checks for canary: require three consecutive successful inference p50 latency under 250ms and error rate <0.5% before proceeding to 50% and then 100%. If any failure, auto-roll back.

I'll edit the MAP to include these as gating criteria. Also suggest we run a short smoke sandbox on a staging tenant 24h before the window.

Irene Choi
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Logan / team — thanks for the clear plan. A few items from Greencliff compliance and ops:

- Window: our preference is not to have work during 00:00–02:00 UTC because we have a nightly batch that runs until ~23:45 PST (04:45 UTC). The 02:00–04:00 UTC window might overlap with shift change for our APAC on-call. Can we propose 03:00–05:00 UTC instead? That keeps work outside our batch and gives us a 2 hour window.

- Evidence: compliance will need the audit export (API audit events + control-plane logs) delivered within 48 hours. Also include an artifact showing the revert (container image IDs + manifest) if a rollback happens.

- Data persistence question: please confirm that telemetry samples and token-level tracing are ephemeral and will not be persisted beyond the standard retention policy (we need this in writing for our security team).

- SLA impact: small concern about increasing cache eviction TTL leading to transient latency spikes — if that happens we will need immediate rollback. Please ensure the revert checklist includes a single-command revert for the cache TTL change.

If you can shift to 03:00–05:00 UTC and add a compliance evidence delivery timeline to the MAP, we can sign the DocuSign by 2026-12-04.

Best,
Alice Kim
VP, Infrastructure Operations | Greencliff Bank
